references.text: In [ref:Luk 22:42|Luke 22:42], Jesus prays intensely that this 'cup' might be taken from him, showing the deep anguish that leads to the intense prayer and sweat drops described in verse 44.

[ref:Heb 5:7|Hebrews 5:7] speaks of how Jesus 'in his days on earth offered prayers and pleas with loud cries and tears to the one who could save him from death' – a clear parallel to Jesus' intense prayer struggle in Gethsemane.
In [ref:Joh 12:27|John 12:27], Jesus says, 'Now my soul is troubled,' showing the same deep inner distress he experienced while preparing for his suffering and death.
[ref:Matt 26:36-39|Matthew 26:36-39] describes Jesus' prayer struggle in Gethsemane where he fell on his face and prayed intensely, paralleling the heartfelt prayer described in Luke.

[ref:Mark 14:33-36|Mark 14:33-36] tells that Jesus began to be deeply distressed and filled with anguish, and asked that the hour might pass from him – Mark's parallel account of the Gethsemane struggle.

In [ref:Matt 26:44|Matthew 26:44], we read that Jesus prayed a third time with the same words, emphasizing the intensity and perseverance in his prayer, paralleling the expression 'he prayed even more earnestly' in Luke 22:44.
[ref:Jes 53:3|Isaiah 53:3] describes the Lord's suffering servant as 'a man of sorrows, familiar with pain,' a prophetic portrayal of the suffering Jesus endured in Gethsemane.

[ref:Sal 22:15|Psalm 22:15] says, 'I am poured out like water … my heart has become like wax; it melts within me' – a messianic psalm that prophetically describes the extreme physical and emotional suffering.

[ref:Sal 69:4|Psalm 69:4] speaks of the sufferer who is exhausted from crying out, a parallel to Jesus' intense prayer struggle where he fought through anguish with a prayer that cost him bloody sweat.

[ref:Luk 22:43|Luke 22:43] tells that an angel from heaven appeared to him and strengthened him – the immediate context showing that God's care and strength were given in the midst of the anguish described in verse 44.
